items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: They were all taught by my uncle.

ctx.x: I know some people have told me that your father and your uncle, especially, would make people study the solfegge for three or four years, maybe before they could take up an instrument.

That's right. Provided with hearing. Hearing. You see, they were great teachers. That's one thing they were. They were great teachers. They turned out many, many, many scholars. They turned out, such as George A. Paquet. He was a famous guy. He was taught by my uncle. And, um, there's, uh, Asheel Batty. They were all taught by my uncle. In better words, my uncle played with Sousa's band. He was clarinating in Sousa's band. Uh-huh. And, uh, later he got in the world, because he just become the big writing and…
Yeah. He'd arrange all of them.
